territory: Letters desk (drafts, autosave, publish, index, reading page, rail module), member-admin message threads (member + admin sides, report threads), notifications (writes, bell, prune, read-marking)

findings.title: "This week in Letters" rail module surfaces city-scoped letters to every member sitewide (content leak + guaranteed 404 on click-through)
findings.expected: A letter published with a city audience ("Bangalore only", set at the letters desk) is visible only to members with a matching UserPlace, everywhere it is surfaced — the letters index and the feed both enforce this via cityScopeWhere.
findings.actual: The feed rail's LettersModule picks the newest main-feed letter with NO viewer context and NO cityScope filter, so a city-scoped letter's title, excerpt, author and read time are shown to every member on /feed. An out-of-city member who clicks it hits the reading page's canViewCityScope check and gets notFound() — a teaser to a 404, for as long as that letter is the newest of the week.
findings.evidence: letters-module.tsx where clause is only: `where: { kind: "letter", isHidden: false, groupId: null, ...PUBLISHED_ONLY, createdAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now() - WEEK_MS) } }` — it selects `title, content, author` and renders `letterTitle(letter.title, letter.content)` plus `plainExcerpt(letter.content)`. Compare letters/page.tsx which adds `...(isAdmin ? {} : { AND: [cityScopeWhere(viewerCities)] })`. The reading page then blocks: `if (!(await canViewCityScope(letter.cityScope, session.user))) notFound();` (letters/[id]/page.tsx:106). FeedRail mounts `<LettersModule />` unconditionally for every viewer (feed-rail.tsx:35). City scope on letters is reachable in practice: LetterDesk passes userPlaces and createPost stores cityScope for non-group letters (feed/actions.ts:119-129).
findings.fixDirection: Pass the viewer (session) into LettersModule (or into FeedRail) and add the same audience filters the letters index uses: `...(isAdmin ? {} : { AND: [cityScopeWhere(viewerCities)] })` plus the targetBatches OR-fragment for symmetry with loadPosts. Since the rail is per-request server-rendered this is one extra Promise.all leg; alternatively query the newest 3 letters and pick the first the viewer may see.
findings.gateOrTest: New unit/integration test: a letter with cityScope='X' and a viewer without X — assert LettersModule renders null / a different letter. Also a Playwright check that the rail teaser never 404s on click for a non-admin member.
findings.reproPlan: Live proof (test accounts): member A (city Bangalore) publishes a letter scoped 'Bangalore only'; member B (no Bangalore UserPlace) loads /feed — the rail shows the letter; clicking it 404s.

findings.title: Every like/comment/reply notification links to /feed#<postId>, which never scrolls to the post and is structurally wrong for group posts and letters
findings.expected: Clicking "X liked your post" / "X commented on your post" lands the member on that content: a letter's thread at /letters/[id], a group post at its group feed, a feed post scrolled into view.
findings.actual: All four write sites hard-code `link: \`/feed#${postId}\`` regardless of the post's kind or groupId. (1) Group posts never appear in the main feed (loadPosts filters `groupId: null`), so the link lands on /feed with nothing to show. (2) A letter's comments are not rendered in the feed (the feed shows a compact letter card; the thread lives at /letters/[id]), so a comment notification on a letter cannot reach the comment. (3) Even for plain feed posts the fragment never works: PostFeed is a client component that fetches posts via the loadPosts server action after mount, so at the moment router.push(notif.link) commits, no element with id=postId exists and there is no hash-handling anywhere in the feed (grep for hash/scrollIntoView in post-feed.tsx returns nothing). The member always lands at the top of the feed. Bonus copy bug: `message: \`${session.user.name} liked your post\`` fires for letters too.
findings.evidence: feed/actions.ts toggleLike: `link: \`/feed#${postId}\`` with only `select: { authorId: true }` on the post (no kind/groupId read); createComment: `link: \`/feed#${parsed.data.postId}\``; reply notification: same; toggleCommentLike: `link: \`/feed#${comment.postId}\``. The anchor exists (`<article id={post.id}>` post-card.tsx:189) but only after client fetch. notification-bell.tsx:168 `router.push(notif.link)`.
findings.fixDirection: At each notification write, read kind and groupId alongside authorId, and build the link: letters -> `/letters/${postId}` (optionally `#comment-<id>`), group posts -> `/groups/${groupId}#${postId}`, feed posts -> `/feed#${postId}` plus a small client hash-handler in PostFeed that, after the first page loads, scrolls to location.hash if present (and ideally fetches the single post by id if it is not on page 1). Fix the copy to say "your letter" when kind=letter.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on the notification writers asserting link shape per kind/groupId; Playwright: like a group post as B, click A's notification, assert URL is the group page and the post is visible.
findings.reproPlan: Live: in a group, member B likes member A's group post; as A, click the bell notification — observe landing on /feed with no such post.

findings.title: Admin bell notifications still deep-link to the retired /admin?thread=<id>#messages, which nothing handles anymore
findings.expected: The admin clicks "X wrote: ..." / "X replied about ..." / "X reported a post ..." in the bell and lands in that conversation (the canonical route is now /admin/messages/[id]; the admin worklist and reports list both link there).
findings.actual: All four notifyAdmins call sites still mint `/admin?thread=${thread.id}#messages`. The admin dashboard page reads no searchParams at all (grep for 'thread' and 'searchParams' in src/app/(main)/admin/page.tsx: zero hits), and no element carries id="messages". The comment in admin/messages/[id]/page.tsx documents the migration: "The notification an admin gets used to point at `/admin?thread=<id>`..." — but the producers were never updated. Every admin notification about member messages and reports lands on the bare dashboard; the sole admin (the owner) hits this on every member contact.
findings.evidence: messages/actions.ts startThread: `await notifyAdmins(..., \`/admin?thread=${thread.id}#messages\`)`; replyToThread: same at :154; report-action.ts reportPost :116 and reportUser :225 identical. Canonical links elsewhere: admin-worklist-query.ts:111 `href: \`/admin/messages/${t.id}\``, report-list.tsx:182 `href={\`/admin/messages/${r.threadId}\`}`.
findings.fixDirection: Change all four notifyAdmins links to `/admin/messages/${threadId}`. Optionally add a redirect in admin/page.tsx from legacy ?thread= for notifications already in the table (they live up to the 100-prune / 365-day retention).
findings.gateOrTest: Grep-based regression check (like security-regressions.test.mjs) pinning that no producer emits '/admin?thread='; or unit test on notifyAdmins call sites.
findings.reproPlan: Live: send a message from a test member account, then as admin click the resulting bell notification — observe landing on /admin dashboard, not the thread.

findings.title: A letter draft's city audience is invisible and unchangeable at the desk: editPost drops cityScope, and the desk never hydrates it
findings.expected: The audience a writer picks at the letters desk is what the letter publishes with, and the desk always shows the draft's current audience.
findings.actual: Three interlocking gaps. (1) editPost's update writes only `{ content, title?, images? }` — cityScope is never read from the form, so choosing a city (or 'Everyone') while resuming a draft is silently ignored. (2) The edit page's select fetches `id, kind, status, authorId, title, content, images, isHidden` — not cityScope — and LetterDesk/CreatePostForm have no initialCityScope prop; `audienceCity` always initialises to null, so a draft saved as 'Bangalore only' renders with no audience chip, looking like 'Everyone'. (3) Even in one sitting: first "Save as draft" stores cityScope via createPost, then onDraftSaved does router.replace to the edit route, remounting the desk with audienceCity reset to null — the chip the writer just set disappears. Net effect: a member can publish a letter believing it goes to everyone when it is city-limited, or believe they limited it when their change was dropped.
findings.evidence: feed/actions.ts editPost: `await prisma.post.update({ where: { id: postId }, data: { content, ...(isLetter ? { title: title?.trim() || null } : {}), ...imagesUpdate } })` — no cityScope. create-post-form.tsx: `const [audienceCity, setAudienceCity] = useState<string | null>(null);` with no initial prop; handleSubmit only does `if (audienceCity) formData.set("cityScope", audienceCity)` which editPost ignores. letters/[id]/edit/page.tsx select list omits cityScope. publishDraft flips status only, preserving whatever cityScope sits on the row.
findings.fixDirection: Fetch cityScope on the edit page, add an initialCityScope prop threaded LetterDesk -> CreatePostForm to seed audienceCity, and make editPost accept a cityScope field for the author's own letter drafts, re-validated against the author's UserPlace list exactly as createPost does (including explicit clearing to null when 'Everyone' is chosen — note the current `if (audienceCity)` guard cannot express clearing; send the field unconditionally for drafts).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: save draft with cityScope, resume, change to Everyone, publish — assert row cityScope is null; and resume-render shows the stored city chip.
findings.reproPlan: Live (test account): at /letters/new pick a city, Save as draft, observe the chip vanish after the route replace; reload /letters/<id>/edit, pick 'Everyone', publish, then query/view as an out-of-city member — the letter is still city-limited.

findings.title: IST members see the wrong calendar date on letters: server-rendered dates use the UTC day
findings.expected: A letter published at 00:30 IST on 21 Aug reads "21 Aug" for its IST readership.
findings.actual: formatDisplayDate and the reading page's inline toLocaleDateString pass no timeZone, and both run in server components (Vercel = UTC), so anything published between 00:00 and 05:30 IST renders the previous day: the letters index byline (`metaLine(batchLine(l.author), formatDisplayDate(l.createdAt))`), the reading page byline (`new Date(letter.createdAt).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })`), and the image-viewer attribution (`date={formatDisplayDate(letter.createdAt)}` computed server-side). Client-side uses (drafts-strip, formatTimeAgo in the bell/threads) are unaffected. This is the deeper IST instance class the bug tracker's raw-SQL note flags as in-scope.
findings.evidence: utils.ts: `return new Date(date).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric" })` — no timeZone option. letters/page.tsx and letters/[id]/page.tsx are async server components (no "use client").
findings.fixDirection: Add `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` to formatDisplayDate and the reading page's inline formatter (the membership is IST by product definition), or move the formatting into a client component. Audit other SERVER call sites of formatDisplayDate at the same time (collection attribution etc.).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test pinning formatDisplayDate(new Date('2026-08-20T19:30:00Z')) === '21 Aug 2026' regardless of process TZ (run tests with TZ=UTC).
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (local dev machine is IST, so the bug only manifests on Vercel UTC; provable by running node with TZ=UTC).

findings.title: Clicking a notification whose row was pruned/retired throws un-caught P2025 and the click silently does nothing (no navigation)
findings.expected: Clicking any notification row always navigates to its link; a row deleted server-side is treated as already-read.
findings.actual: markNotificationRead uses `prisma.notification.update({ where: { id: notificationId, userId: session.user.id }, ... })` with no P2025 handling — update throws when no row matches. The bell's handler does `await markNotificationRead(notif.id)` BEFORE `router.push(notif.link)` with no try/catch, so the rejection aborts the handler: the member clicks and nothing happens. Rows under a displayed panel can vanish: (a) the 100-prune runs on every first-page bell open on ANY device, deleting rows beyond the 100th — a second device's panel scrolled past 100 now holds dead rows; (b) the nightly retention sweep deletes rows older than 365 days while a panel is open.
findings.evidence: notifications/actions.ts:77-84 has no try/catch and no updateMany; notification-bell.tsx:160-171: `if (!notif.read) { await markNotificationRead(notif.id); ... } if (notif.link) { router.push(notif.link); }`. Prune: `await prisma.notification.deleteMany({ where: { userId, createdAt: { lt: cutoff[0].createdAt } } })`. Retention: `prisma.notification.deleteMany({ where: { createdAt: { lt: cutoff(365) } } })`.
findings.fixDirection: Switch markNotificationRead to `updateMany({ where: { id, userId, read: false } })` (idempotent, never throws on missing rows), or wrap in try/catch; in the bell, navigate regardless of the mark call's outcome (fire the mark without blocking router.push).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: markNotificationRead on a nonexistent id resolves without throwing.
findings.reproPlan: Live: delete a notification row directly is a write — instead prove with two sessions: open bell and scroll past 100 rows on device A, open bell on device B (prune fires), click an old row on A; observe dead click in console.

findings.title: Bell unread badge is a page-load snapshot, desynced from the panel it opens; revalidatePath("/") purges nothing members are on
findings.expected: The badge count and the "Mark all read" affordance agree with the rows the panel actually shows.
findings.actual: initialUnreadCount is computed once (layout/feed page render) and only ever mutated locally. handleOpen re-fetches the first PAGE on every open but never reconciles the count, and getNotifications does not return one. Concrete desyncs a member will see: (1) notifications arriving after page load show as highlighted unread rows in the panel while the badge shows 0 and the "Mark all read" button is absent (`{unreadCount > 0 && (<button ...Mark all read)}`) — the only way to un-highlight them is clicking each one; (2) after reading on the phone, the desktop badge keeps its stale count indefinitely (no polling; and the actions' `revalidatePath("/")` targets only the route "/" — members live under /feed, /letters, etc., and a layout-wide purge would need revalidatePath("/", "layout")); (3) double-clicking one unread row decrements the badge twice (both click handlers read the pre-render `notif.read === false`). Also the decaying shake-on-rise animation is dead code in practice, since unreadCount can never rise client-side.
findings.evidence: bell: `const [unreadCount, setUnreadCount] = useState(initialUnreadCount);` — the only setters are the local decrements/zeroing; handleOpen sets notifications/nextCursor/hasMore/loaded only. notifications/actions.ts markNotificationRead/markAllNotificationsRead: `revalidatePath("/")`. Layout count: prisma.notification.count({ where: { userId, read: false } }) at layout render.
findings.fixDirection: Return the unread count from getNotifications (one extra count query, or derive from page-1 rows plus a count) and setUnreadCount on every open; make handleClickNotification idempotent per id; drop the ineffective revalidatePath("/") calls or change to ("/", "layout") if a server-driven refresh is actually wanted.
findings.gateOrTest: Component test: open panel with fresh unread rows and initialUnreadCount=0 — assert Mark-all-read renders and badge matches row state.
findings.reproPlan: Live: sign in on two browsers; generate a like for user A from user B; without navigating, open A's bell — rows highlight but badge stays 0 and no Mark-all-read button.

findings.title: createPost accepts 20,000-char plain posts but editPost caps posts at 5,000 — long posts become permanently uneditable
findings.expected: One cap per kind, enforced identically on create and edit (spec: 5,000 for posts, 20,000 for letters), with the composer surfacing the limit.
findings.actual: postSchema validates `content: z.string().min(1).max(20000)` for BOTH kinds, while editPost enforces `const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000`. The composer has no counter or client cap (only the soft letter nudge at 600 chars), so a member can write and publish a 6,000-20,000 char plain post — and then can never edit it: every edit attempt returns "Content must be between 1 and 5000 characters" even for a one-word typo fix, because editPost validates the full body.
findings.evidence: validators.ts:154: `content: z.string().min(1, "Post cannot be empty").max(20000),` with no kind-conditional refine. feed/actions.ts:396-399: `const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000; if (!content || content.length > cap) { return { error: ... } }`. create-post-form.tsx has no maxLength on the contentEditable and no counter (LETTER_NUDGE_LEN is a hint only).
findings.fixDirection: Add a superRefine to postSchema: content ≤ 5000 when kind !== 'letter' (createPost then matches editPost), and surface a counter in the composer past ~4500 chars for posts. Decide what to do for already-stored oversize posts (grandfather them in editPost by only enforcing the cap when length grew, or migrate).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: postSchema rejects kind='post' content of 5001 chars; editPost accepts an edit that does not grow an oversize legacy row.
findings.reproPlan: Live (test account): paste 6,000 chars into the composer, Post (succeeds), then Edit and change one character (fails with the 5000 error).

findings.title: Two tabs/devices editing the same letter draft silently clobber each other (autosave last-write-wins, no version check)
findings.expected: Concurrent editing of one draft either merges, blocks, or at least warns; a stale surface cannot silently destroy newer writing.
findings.actual: The desk autosaves the FULL body 2.5s after any keystroke via editPost, which does an unconditional `prisma.post.update` with no updatedAt/version precondition. A member with the draft open on laptop and phone who writes three paragraphs on the laptop, then later taps one character on the still-open phone tab, has the phone's stale full content overwrite everything — no warning, and the desk on both devices says "Saved".
findings.evidence: Autosave effect: `fd.set("content", content); ... const result = await editPost(postId, fd);` — whole-document write. editPost: `await prisma.post.update({ where: { id: postId }, data: { content, ... } })` — no `updatedAt` guard, no baseUpdatedAt token from the client.
findings.fixDirection: Send the draft's updatedAt (from page load / last successful save) with each editPost call and make the update conditional (`updateMany({ where: { id, authorId, updatedAt: base } })`); on 0 rows updated, surface "This letter changed somewhere else — reload before continuing" instead of overwriting.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on editPost with a stale base timestamp returning a conflict; manual two-tab check.
findings.reproPlan: Live (test account): open the same draft in two tabs, type in tab A (autosaves), type one char in tab B, reload — tab A's writing is gone.

findings.title: Letters desk autosave fails silently: errors leave "Saving..." stuck forever and the writer keeps writing into a draft that is no longer being saved
findings.expected: If autosave stops working (session expired, content over the 20,000 cap, network/DB error), the desk says so; the status line never lies.
findings.actual: The autosave callback does `onAutosaveState?.("saving"); ... const result = await editPost(postId, fd); if (!result.error) onAutosaveState?.("saved");` — on ANY error the state is left at "Saving..." permanently and nothing else happens: no toast, no retry, no distinction between transient and permanent failure. A letter that crosses 20,000 chars stops autosaving forever with no signal (editPost returns the cap error on every subsequent tick). If editPost THROWS (network drop), the rejection is unhandled inside setTimeout — same stuck state plus an unhandled rejection. Secondary defect: the in-flight guard `if (submitting || savingDraft) return;` reads STALE closure values — the effect's deps are `[content, title, images, postId]`, so a Publish click after the last keystroke does not refresh or cancel the pending timer, and the autosave editPost can run concurrently with publishDraft (benign today only because the payloads are identical).
findings.evidence: Effect at create-post-form.tsx:209-232; deps comment: `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n  }, [content, title, images, postId]);` — submitting/savingDraft excluded; no catch around `await editPost`; no error branch after `if (!result.error)`.
findings.fixDirection: Add an error path: set a third autosave state ("error", shown as 'Not saved — check your connection' with the last-saved time), wrap the await in try/catch, and clear the pending timer when submitting/savingDraft flips (add them to deps or clear the timer inside handleSubmit). Treat the over-cap error specially (surface the count).
findings.gateOrTest: Component test: editPost mock returning {error} — assert the desk leaves 'Saving...' and shows the failure state.
findings.reproPlan: Live: resume a draft, kill the network, type — 'Saving...' stays forever with no error.

findings.title: A fresh unsaved letter has zero navigation guard: back-swipe, the back link, or a closed tab discards the entire piece silently
findings.expected: A page whose whole purpose is long-form writing warns before discarding unsaved text (beforeunload + in-app navigation confirm), or autosaves from the first keystroke.
findings.actual: Autosave only runs `if (!postId)`-never for a FRESH letter (comment: "a fresh letter has no row to update until the first explicit Save as draft"), and there is no beforeunload handler anywhere in the repo (grep for beforeunload: zero hits). The desk's "All letters" back link is always active. A member 40 minutes into a letter who back-swipes on a phone, taps the back link, or lets the tab die loses everything with no prompt. The composer's outside-click guard only prevents pill-collapse, not navigation, and doesn't apply to the immersive desk at all.
findings.evidence: letter-desk.tsx renders a plain `<Link href="/letters">` above the sheet; create-post-form.tsx autosave effect begins `if (!postId) return;`; repo-wide grep `beforeunload|onbeforeunload` returns nothing.
findings.fixDirection: Register a beforeunload handler while `content.trim() && !postId && dirty` on the desk (and ideally while a resumed draft has unsaved changes), and intercept the back link with a confirm when dirty. Better still: create the draft row automatically on the first pause (first autosave tick creates via createPost saveAsDraft and adopts the id through the existing onDraftSaved path), which the plumbing already supports.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright: type into /letters/new, trigger navigation, assert the confirm appears (or that a draft row exists).
findings.reproPlan: Live: type a paragraph at /letters/new, click 'All letters' — content is gone, no prompt, no draft row.

findings.title: /notice/[id] legacy resolver is non-idempotent: concurrent or retried opens mint duplicate "Notes from the admins" threads
findings.expected: Resolving an old admin_note notification into a thread happens exactly once per notification, however many times or how concurrently the page is opened.
findings.actual: The page does check-then-create-then-update during a GET render with no idempotency key: `if (notification.link?.startsWith("/messages/")) redirect(...)` else `openAdminNoticeThread(...)` then `notification.update({ link, read: true })`. Two concurrent first opens (two tabs, a double-tap, or a retried request) both pass the link check and both create a thread — the member's /messages list then shows the same moderation note twice, each a full 'notice' AdminThread with memberUnread=true. If the notification.update fails after the create, EVERY future open creates yet another thread. AdminThread has no unique key tying it to the source notification, so the database cannot stop this.
findings.evidence: notice/[id]/page.tsx:36-48 quoted above; openAdminNoticeThread is a bare `prisma.adminThread.create`. No transaction, no unique constraint on (memberId, kind, subject) or a sourceNotificationId.
findings.fixDirection: Make resolution idempotent: first `updateMany({ where: { id, link: null (or not-yet-/messages/) }, data: { link: RESOLVING } })`-style claim, or store the thread id on the notification inside one $transaction with the create; simplest: add a nullable unique `sourceNotificationId` column on AdminThread and upsert on it.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: call the resolution logic twice concurrently for one notification; assert one thread.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (needs a legacy admin_note row with a /notice link; racing writes on prod data is not acceptable).

findings.title: Letters index silently truncates at 40 with no pagination — older letters vanish from the archive surface
findings.expected: The letters page is the archive of long-form pieces; every published letter stays reachable from it (paginated or 'load more').
findings.actual: `take: 40` with `orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }` and no cursor, no 'More letters' affordance, no count — the 41st-newest letter simply stops existing on /letters. At 2,000 members this is months away, and unlike the feed there is no infinite scroll fallback on this page (old letters remain findable only via feed scroll or search). The drafts strip has the same shape (take: 20) — a 21st draft is invisible but still occupies a row.
findings.evidence: letters/page.tsx: `orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }, take: 40,` then `letters.map((l) => (...))` with nothing rendered after the list. Drafts: `take: 20`.
findings.fixDirection: Add keyset pagination (same (createdAt,id) pattern as loadPosts) with a 'More letters' button or infinite scroll; at minimum a link to the feed pre-filtered to kind=letter. For drafts, 20 is fine but consider a count so 'you have 23 drafts' is at least visible.
findings.gateOrTest: Seed 41 letters in a test DB; assert the 41st is reachable from /letters.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (production has fewer than 40 letters today; the truncation is arithmetic).

findings.title: The 100-notification prune deletes UNREAD rows, including moderation/admin notices the member never saw
findings.expected: Per the brief's explicit question: whether the prune can destroy unread signal. High-importance rows (admin_note, admin_message, report_update) should outlive a flood of likes, or unread rows should be exempt.
findings.actual: The prune keys purely on recency: `deleteMany({ where: { userId, createdAt: { lt: cutoff[0].createdAt } } })` with the cutoff at the 100th-newest row regardless of read state or type. A member whose letter draws 100+ like/comment notifications before they next open the bell loses every older UNREAD row — including an admin_note attached to a removed post. The signal partially survives elsewhere (the AdminThread still sits in /messages with memberUnread=true), but the notification channel for it is silently destroyed, and the unread count self-corrects only on the next layout render. Off-by-one and tie-handling are clean (skip KEEP-1/take 1; `lt` keeps ties), and the prune correctly skips cursored pages.
findings.evidence: actions.ts:44-57 quoted; no `read` or `type` condition in either the cutoff query or the deleteMany.
findings.fixDirection: Either exempt unread rows (`read: true` in the deleteMany where, accepting slower shrink for hoarders), or exempt the admin/moderation types, or both: delete read rows past 100 plus unread rows past a larger ceiling (e.g. 500).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: 150 rows, rows 120-150 unread admin_note — open bell, assert admin_note rows survive.

findings.title: Thread pages load every message with no take: an unbounded query on both the member and admin conversation views
findings.expected: Bounded reads on every list (2,000-user headroom rule): a conversation view pages or windows its messages.
findings.actual: Both thread pages fetch `messages: { orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" }, select: {...} }` with no take. The per-member throttle is 40 messages/hour ACROSS all threads (isMessageRateLimited counts by authorId), so one long-running conversation can legally accumulate thousands of rows over months; each open then serializes the entire history (bodies up to 4,000 chars each) into one RSC payload. Retention deletes messages older than 730 days, which caps growth eventually but leaves plenty of room for a multi-MB page. The admin list page correctly loads headers+last message only, so this is the one unbounded read in the messages feature.
findings.evidence: messages/[id]/page.tsx:40-52 — no take on the messages include; admin-threads-server.ts:35-41 shows the rate limit is per-author, not per-thread; retention.ts adminMessages: 730 days.
findings.fixDirection: Add `take: -200` (last 200) with an 'earlier messages' loader, or plain take with keyset paging — the Conversation component already receives a flat array so windowing is contained.
findings.gateOrTest: Seed a 1,000-message thread in a test DB; assert page payload stays bounded.

findings.title: Letter view telemetry (recordView) fires before the visibility checks and is un-awaited on serverless
findings.expected: A 'view' is recorded only for letters the viewer is actually allowed to read, and the write reliably lands.
findings.actual: `void recordView(session.user.id, "letter", letter.id);` runs after only the kind/isHidden check but BEFORE the draft-author, group-membership and city-scope gates — a non-author probing a draft id, or a non-member hitting a group letter, is counted as a reader of content they were refused (the analytics this exists for, 'read click-through rates', over-count). Separately, the promise is fired-and-forgotten without after(): it usually completes because the render continues through further awaits, but on the fast path (all checks cached/fast) the lambda can freeze before the upsert commits, dropping views. Prisma upsert's find-then-create race under two concurrent first views throws P2002, which the internal catch swallows in production — acceptable, but development-only logging means a production failure mode is invisible.
findings.evidence: letters/[id]/page.tsx: recordView at :85, `if (isDraft && !isAuthor) notFound();` at :93, group check at :96-102, city check at :106. content-view.ts catch: `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") console.error(...)`.
findings.fixDirection: Move the recordView call below all three visibility gates, and wrap it in `after(() => recordView(...))` so it survives the response without delaying it.

findings.title: letterTitle and the letters-index excerpt leave a stray "!" for letters opening with image markdown — the exact bug already fixed in plainExcerpt
findings.expected: All three teaser/title derivations strip image markdown identically (plainExcerpt's comment records the '!banyan' bug and fixes it by stripping `![alt](url)` BEFORE the link rule).
findings.actual: letterTitle (used by the letters index heading, the reading page title/metadata, and the feed letter card) and the letters index's local excerpt() both run only `.replace(/[*_#>`~]|\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)/g, "$1")` — `![photo](url)` becomes `!photo`, so an untitled letter that opens with a hand-typed image renders '!photo...' as its title and its excerpt. plainExcerpt has the fix (`.replace(/!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)/g, "")` first); the other two derivations were never updated, so the same content shows a clean teaser in the rail and a glitched title on the index.
findings.evidence: utils.ts letterTitle:349-357 lacks the image rule; utils.ts plainExcerpt:377-390 has it with the comment "They used to fall through to the link rule below and leave a stray '!'"; letters/page.tsx excerpt():22-28 duplicates the un-fixed regex.
findings.fixDirection: Apply the same image-strip-first rule in letterTitle and replace the letters page's local excerpt() with plainExcerpt(content, 240) so there is one derivation.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: letterTitle(null, '![banyan](url)\nreal first line') === 'real first line'.
findings.reproPlan: Live (test account): publish an untitled letter starting with `![banyan](x)` and view /letters.
